content.comment_body: [company_name] devices of [product_name] [version_no] BM (including SIPLUS variants) have a vulnerability that permits electromagnetic fault injection. This vulnerability could allow attackers to access and debug the firmware, as well as manipulate device memory. Attackers might also inject public keys from custom-generated key pairs, which are then signed by the [product_name] [version_no] Product CA. The underlying issue is linked to the specific hardware design of the [product_name] [version_no] BM. [company_name] has addressed this vulnerability with updated hardware in the [product_name] [version_no] BM product line, rotating the Product CA private key. The company continues to develop hardware improvements for affected device variations, such as SIPLUS, to resolve the issue further. More details are available in the "Additional Information" section.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants express concern about a significant security flaw in [product_name] [version_no] BM hardware, which enables attackers to use electromagnetic fault injection methods, threatening firmware integrity and cryptographic protections. The exploit allows advanced manipulation—such as the insertion of attacker-generated keys signed by the device's certificate authority. While [company_name] has addressed the issue in newer hardware versions, the schedule for updates or fixes for certain variants, including SIPLUS, has not yet been disclosed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] products to maintain strong security against hardware-based attacks and to release prompt updates or fixes for all affected variants when vulnerabilities are identified.
